title: The Dhammapada
author: The Buddha (trad.)
translator: F. Max Müller, 1881 (public domain, Project Gutenberg #2017)
blurb: Short verses from the Buddha's teaching on the mind: what you think, you become.

earnestness.e: Her earnestness in practice made her the best in class.

nirvana.m: In Buddhism, freedom from suffering and desire.
nirvana.e: Monks meditate for years seeking nirvana.

fletcher.e: The fletcher straightened each arrow over a flame.

liberality.e: His liberality helped the whole village build a well.

passion.e: Passion for music kept him practising daily.

cards.title: You are your thoughts
cards.text: The Dhammapada begins with the mind. Everything we are comes from what we think. Act from a bad thought and pain follows like a cart wheel behind an ox; act from a pure one and happiness follows like a shadow.
cards.quote: All that we are is the result of what we have thought: it is founded on our thoughts, it is made up of our thoughts.
cards.qMean: Your life is shaped by your thoughts.
cards.qLife: Thinking 'I'm bad at maths' makes you stop trying — and so you stay bad at it.
cards.cap: Seated Buddha from India · public domain

cards.title: Hatred never ends hatred
cards.text: Answering hatred with hatred keeps it going forever. Only love — or friendliness — brings it to an end. This, says the Buddha, is an ancient law.
cards.quote: For hatred does not cease by hatred at any time: hatred ceases by love, this is an old rule.
cards.qMean: Hate never stops hate; only love stops it.
cards.qLife: Ending a family feud by being the first to apologise.
cards.cap: Ajanta painting, National Museum, New Delhi · public domain

cards.title: A well-thatched roof
cards.text: Rain leaks through a badly thatched roof; desire leaks into a mind that never reflects. A mind that pauses and thinks keeps passion out, like a good roof keeps out the rain.
cards.quote: As rain breaks through an ill-thatched house, passion will break through an unreflecting mind.
cards.qMean: A careless mind lets cravings in, like rain through a bad roof.
cards.qLife: Impulse-buying everything in the cart because you never stopped to think.
cards.cap: Thatched huts by a river, Bengal · public domain

cards.title: Wakefulness is life
cards.text: Alert, careful effort leads to freedom; carelessness is a kind of death. Those who stay awake to their lives truly live; the thoughtless are as if already dead.
cards.quote: Earnestness is the path of immortality (Nirvana), thoughtlessness the path of death.
cards.qMean: Paying careful attention leads to freedom; carelessness leads to ruin.
cards.qLife: Reading the contract carefully instead of clicking 'agree'.

cards.title: Straighten the mind
cards.text: The mind trembles and wanders like a fish thrown on dry land. A wise person straightens it the way an arrow-maker straightens an arrow — patiently, with skill.
cards.quote: As a fletcher makes straight his arrow, a wise man makes straight his trembling and unsteady thought
cards.qMean: A wise person steadies their restless mind like an arrow-maker straightens an arrow.
cards.qLife: Bringing your attention back to the page every time your phone buzzes.

cards.title: The wise fool
cards.text: A fool who knows he is a fool is at least that much wise; the real fool is the one who thinks himself wise.
cards.quote: The fool who knows his foolishness, is wise at least so far.
cards.qMean: Knowing you don't know is a kind of wisdom.
cards.qLife: The new employee who asks questions learns faster than the one who pretends.
cards.cap: Jataka tales, illustrated manuscript · public domain

cards.title: Like a rock
cards.text: A solid rock is not moved by the wind; the wise are not moved by praise or blame. They stay calm and clear like a deep lake.
cards.quote: As a solid rock is not shaken by the wind, wise people falter not amidst blame and praise.
cards.qMean: Wise people stay steady whether they are praised or criticised.
cards.qLife: Reading both good and bad comments on your work without your mood swinging.
cards.cap: Sculpture of Buddha Muchalinda, NUS Museum · public domain

cards.title: The greatest victory
cards.text: Winning a thousand battles is less than winning over yourself. Self-mastery is a victory nobody can take away.
cards.quote: If one man conquer in battle a thousand times thousand men, and if another conquer himself, he is the greatest of conquerors.
cards.qMean: Beating your own weaknesses is greater than beating any army.
cards.qLife: Quitting smoking is a bigger win than any argument you ever won.

cards.title: Answer anger with love
cards.text: Overcome anger with kindness, evil with good, greed with generosity, and lies with truth.
cards.quote: Let a man overcome anger by love, let him overcome evil by good; let him overcome the greedy by liberality, the liar by truth!
cards.qMean: Beat anger with love, greed with generosity, and lies with truth.
cards.qLife: Replying calmly and kindly to an angry customer until they calm down too.
